events.title: First Ancient Olympics
events.description: The first recorded Olympic Games are held in Olympia, Greece, featuring a single footrace.

events.title: Theodosius I Bans the Games
events.description: Emperor Theodosius I bans all pagan festivals, including the Olympics, ending the ancient cycle.

events.title: Cotswold Olimpick Games
events.description: Robert Dover founds the Cotswold Olimpick Games in England, an early precursor to the modern revival.

events.title: IOC Founded
events.description: Pierre de Coubertin founds the International Olympic Committee at the Sorbonne in Paris.

events.title: First Modern Summer Olympics
events.description: The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens, Greece, with 241 athletes from 14 nations.

events.title: First Marathon Winner
events.description: Spyridon Louis wins the first modern marathon at the Athens Games.

events.title: Paris 1900 Olympics
events.description: The second modern Games are held in Paris as part of the World's Fair, featuring the first female competitors.

events.title: First Female Olympic Champion
events.description: Charlotte Cooper wins the tennis singles in Paris, becoming the first individual female Olympic champion.

events.title: St. Louis 1904 Olympics
events.description: The Games are held in St. Louis, Missouri; the first time gold, silver, and bronze medals are awarded.

events.title: London 1908 Olympics
events.description: London hosts the Games; the marathon distance is standardized to 26 miles and 385 yards.

events.title: Stockholm 1912 Olympics
events.description: Stockholm hosts the 'Swedish Masterpiece' Games, featuring electronic timing for the first time.

events.title: Jim Thorpe's Double Gold
events.description: Jim Thorpe wins both the pentathlon and decathlon in Stockholm, though his medals are later stripped and eventually restored.

events.title: 1916 Games Cancelled
events.description: The Berlin 1916 Summer Olympics are cancelled due to the outbreak of World War I.

events.title: Antwerp 1920 Olympics
events.description: The Olympic Flag and the Olympic Oath are introduced for the first time in Antwerp, Belgium.

events.title: First Winter Olympics
events.description: The 'International Winter Sports Week' is held in Chamonix, France, later recognized as the first Winter Olympics.

events.title: Paris 1924 Summer Olympics
events.description: The 'Chariots of Fire' Games see Paavo Nurmi win five gold medals in middle and long-distance running.

events.title: St. Moritz 1928 Winter Olympics
events.description: The second Winter Games are held in Switzerland, the first to be held in a different nation than the Summer Games of the same year.

events.title: Amsterdam 1928 Summer Olympics
events.description: The Olympic Flame is lit for the first time in the modern era, and Greece leads the parade of nations.

events.title: Lake Placid 1932 Winter Olympics
events.description: The Winter Games are held in the US for the first time; Sonja Henie wins her second figure skating gold.

events.title: Los Angeles 1932 Summer Olympics
events.description: The first Olympic Village is built, and the 16-day format for the Games is established.

events.title: Garmisch-Partenkirchen 1936 Winter Games
events.description: Alpine skiing is included in the Olympic program for the first time.

events.title: Berlin 1936 Summer Olympics
events.description: The Games are opened by Adolf Hitler; Jesse Owens wins four gold medals, defying Nazi racial theories.

events.title: First Torch Relay
events.description: The first Olympic torch relay is held, carrying the flame from Olympia to Berlin.

events.title: 1940 & 1944 Games Cancelled
events.description: Both Summer and Winter Games are cancelled for 1940 and 1944 due to World War II.

events.title: St. Moritz 1948 Winter Olympics
events.description: The first post-war Olympics are held in Switzerland, known as the 'Games of Renewal'.

events.title: London 1948 Summer Olympics
events.description: The 'Austerity Games' are held in war-torn London; Fanny Blankers-Koen wins four gold medals.

events.title: Oslo 1952 Winter Olympics
events.description: The Winter Games are held in the capital of Norway, featuring the first Olympic torch relay for a Winter Games.

events.title: Helsinki 1952 Summer Olympics
events.description: The Soviet Union competes for the first time, and Emil Zátopek wins three distance gold medals.

events.title: Cortina d'Ampezzo 1956 Winter Games
events.description: The first Winter Games to be televised, and the first time the Olympic Oath is taken by a woman.

events.title: Melbourne 1956 Summer Olympics
events.description: The first Games held in the Southern Hemisphere; equestrian events are held in Stockholm due to quarantine laws.

events.title: Squaw Valley 1960 Winter Olympics
events.description: Walt Disney directs the opening and closing ceremonies; IBM provides the first electronic data processing for the Games.

events.title: Rome 1960 Summer Olympics
events.description: Abebe Bikila wins the marathon barefoot; Muhammad Ali (Cassius Clay) wins gold in light heavyweight boxing.

events.title: Innsbruck 1964 Winter Olympics
events.description: Snow is trucked in by the Austrian army due to a lack of snowfall.

events.title: Tokyo 1964 Summer Olympics
events.description: The first Games held in Asia; they are the first to be broadcast internationally via satellite.

events.title: Grenoble 1968 Winter Olympics
events.description: The first Games to include gender testing and drug testing.

events.title: Mexico City 1968 Summer Olympics
events.description: Tommie Smith and John Carlos perform the Black Power salute; Bob Beamon sets a long jump record that lasts 23 years.

events.title: Sapporo 1972 Winter Olympics
events.description: The first Winter Games held outside Europe and North America.

events.title: Munich 1972 Summer Olympics
events.description: Mark Spitz wins seven gold medals in swimming; the Games are marred by the Munich massacre terrorist attack.

events.title: Innsbruck 1976 Winter Olympics
events.description: Innsbruck hosts for a second time after Denver, Colorado, withdraws due to costs and environmental concerns.

events.title: Montreal 1976 Summer Olympics
events.description: Nadia Comăneci scores the first perfect 10.0 in Olympic gymnastics history.

events.title: Lake Placid 1980 Winter Olympics
events.description: The 'Miracle on Ice' occurs as the US men's hockey team defeats the heavily favored Soviet Union.

events.title: Moscow 1980 Summer Olympics
events.description: The US leads a boycott of 65 nations to protest the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.

events.title: Sarajevo 1984 Winter Olympics
events.description: The Games are held in Yugoslavia; Torvill and Dean receive perfect scores for their 'Bolero' ice dance.

events.title: Los Angeles 1984 Summer Olympics
events.description: The Soviet Union leads a retaliatory boycott; Carl Lewis wins four gold medals, matching Jesse Owens.

events.title: Calgary 1988 Winter Olympics
events.description: The Games are extended to 16 days; the Jamaican bobsled team and Eddie 'The Eagle' Edwards become sensations.

events.title: Seoul 1988 Summer Olympics
events.description: Ben Johnson sets a world record in the 100m but is disqualified for doping, a major turning point in drug testing.

events.title: Albertville 1992 Winter Olympics
events.description: The last time Winter and Summer Games are held in the same year.

events.title: Barcelona 1992 Summer Olympics
events.description: The 'Dream Team' US basketball squad dominates; South Africa returns to the Games after the end of apartheid.

events.title: Lillehammer 1994 Winter Olympics
events.description: The first Winter Games held in a different year than the Summer Games; the Kerrigan-Harding skating scandal dominates headlines.

events.title: Atlanta 1996 Summer Olympics
events.description: The Centennial Games; Muhammad Ali lights the cauldron; Michael Johnson wins the 200m and 400m double.

events.title: Nagano 1998 Winter Olympics
events.description: Snowboarding and women's ice hockey make their Olympic debuts.

events.title: Sydney 2000 Summer Olympics
events.description: Cathy Freeman lights the cauldron and wins the 400m; North and South Korea march together under one flag.

events.title: Salt Lake City 2002 Winter Games
events.description: The Games are held under high security following 9/11; a judging scandal in figure skating leads to two gold medals.

events.title: Athens 2004 Summer Olympics
events.description: The Games return to their birthplace; Michael Phelps wins eight medals, including six gold.

events.title: Turin 2006 Winter Olympics
events.description: Italy hosts for a second time; Shaun White wins his first snowboarding gold.

events.title: Beijing 2008 Summer Olympics
events.description: Usain Bolt sets three world records; Michael Phelps wins a record eight gold medals in a single Games.

events.title: Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics
events.description: The Games are held in British Columbia; Canada wins a record 14 gold medals at a Winter Games.

events.title: London 2012 Summer Olympics
events.description: London becomes the first city to host three times; women's boxing is included for the first time.

events.title: Sochi 2014 Winter Olympics
events.description: The most expensive Games to date, held on the Black Sea coast and in the Caucasus Mountains.

events.title: Rio 2016 Summer Olympics
events.description: The first Games held in South America; the Refugee Olympic Team competes for the first time.

events.title: PyeongChang 2018 Winter Olympics
events.description: Nigeria and Eritrea send athletes to the Winter Games for the first time.

events.title: Tokyo 2020 (2021) Olympics
events.description: The Games are postponed by one year due to the COVID-19 pandemic, held mostly without spectators.

events.title: Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics
events.description: Beijing becomes the first city to host both Summer and Winter Olympics.

events.title: Paris 2024 Summer Olympics
events.description: Paris hosts for the third time, exactly 100 years after its second host year.

events.title: First Olympic Esports Week
events.description: The IOC holds the inaugural Olympic Esports Week in Singapore, exploring the future of virtual sports.

events.title: Los Angeles 1984: Rafer Johnson Lights Cauldron
events.description: The decathlon champion lights the torch at the Coliseum in a memorable opening ceremony.

events.title: Seoul 1988: Flo-Jo's Sprint Dominance
events.description: Florence Griffith-Joyner wins three gold medals and sets long-standing records in the 100m and 200m.

events.title: Barcelona 1992: Derek Redmond Finish
events.description: Derek Redmond, helped by his father, finishes his 400m semi-final after tearing his hamstring, in a classic Olympic moment.

events.title: Atlanta 1996: Kerri Strug's Vault
events.description: Strug sticks her vault on an injured ankle to clinch the first-ever team gold for US women's gymnastics.

events.title: Sydney 2000: Eric the Eel
events.description: Eric Moussambani of Equatorial Guinea becomes a crowd favorite for his slow but determined 100m freestyle swim.

events.title: Salt Lake 2002: Vonetta Flowers Gold
events.description: Bobsledder Vonetta Flowers becomes the first Black athlete to win a gold medal at a Winter Olympics.

events.title: Athens 2004: Kelly Holmes Double
events.description: British runner Kelly Holmes wins both the 800m and 1500m gold medals.

events.title: Beijing 2008: Bolt's 100m Record
events.description: Usain Bolt wins the 100m in 9.69 seconds, even while celebrating before the finish line.

events.title: London 2012: Mo Farah's Super Saturday
events.description: Mo Farah wins the 10,000m on a night where Great Britain wins three athletics golds in 44 minutes.

events.title: Rio 2016: Simone Biles Dominance
events.description: Simone Biles wins four gold medals, cementing her status as one of the greatest gymnasts ever.

events.title: Tokyo 2020: High Jump Shared Gold
events.description: Mutaz Barshim and Gianmarco Tamberi agree to share the gold medal in the men's high jump.

events.title: First Winter Games to be Professionally Open
events.description: The IOC begins allowing professional athletes to compete, leading to the end of the strict amateurism era.

events.title: The First Paralympic Games
events.description: The first official Paralympic Games are held in Rome, following the Summer Olympics.

events.title: The First Youth Olympic Games
events.description: The inaugural Youth Olympic Games are held in Singapore for athletes aged 14 to 18.

events.title: IOC Headquarters Move to Olympic House
events.description: The IOC inaugurates its new, sustainable headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland, on Olympic Day.

events.title: First Olympic Boycott
events.description: Several nations boycott the Melbourne Games due to the Suez Crisis and the Soviet invasion of Hungary.

events.title: The 1906 Intercalated Games
events.description: Held in Athens to revitalize the movement; though successful, they are not officially recognized by the IOC today.

events.title: Introduction of the Olympic Mascot
events.description: Schuss, a stylized skier, becomes the first (unofficial) Olympic mascot at the Grenoble Winter Games.

events.title: First Official Mascot: Waldi
events.description: Waldi the dachshund becomes the first official Olympic mascot for the Munich Summer Games.

events.title: The Refugee Olympic Team
events.description: The IOC creates the Refugee Olympic Team (ROT) to allow displaced athletes to compete under the Olympic flag.

events.title: Hajo Seppelt Doping Documentary
events.description: A German documentary exposes state-sponsored doping in Russia, leading to massive sanctions and the OAR designation.

events.title: The 1920 Opening: Release of Doves
events.description: The tradition of releasing doves as a symbol of peace begins at the Antwerp Games.

events.title: First Appearance of the Olympic Rings
events.description: The Olympic flag, designed by Coubertin in 1913, is flown for the first time at the Antwerp Games.

events.title: Paavo Nurmi Lights 1952 Cauldron
events.description: The legendary Finnish runner lights the flame in Helsinki to a standing ovation.

events.title: The first Olympic village (Women)
events.description: Women athletes are housed in the Chapman Park Hotel during the LA Games, while men stay in the first purpose-built village.

events.title: The 'Blood in the Water' Match
events.description: A violent water polo match between Hungary and the USSR takes place shortly after the Hungarian Revolution.

events.title: Wilma Rudolph's Three Golds
events.description: After surviving polio as a child, Wilma Rudolph wins three gold medals in track in Rome.

events.title: Dick Fosbury's Flop
events.description: Dick Fosbury wins high jump gold with his new back-first 'Fosbury Flop' technique.

events.title: Mark Spitz: Seven World Records
events.description: Spitz wins seven gold medals in Munich, setting a world record in every single event.

events.title: The First Winter Olympic Gold for China
events.description: Yang Yang (A) wins the 500m short track speed skating, China's first-ever Winter Olympic gold.

events.title: Michael Phelps: 23rd Gold
events.description: Phelps swims his final Olympic race in Rio, finishing with a record-shattering 23 gold medals.

events.title: Yuzuru Hanyu: Back-to-Back Gold
events.description: The Japanese skater becomes the first man in 66 years to win consecutive Olympic titles in figure skating.

events.title: Sky Brown: Youngest GB Medalist
events.description: At age 13, Sky Brown wins bronze in skateboarding's Olympic debut in Tokyo.

events.title: The first Modern Games Marathon
events.description: The event was inspired by the legend of Pheidippides and run from the city of Marathon to Athens.

events.title: Inclusion of Golf and Rugby Sevens
events.description: Golf returns after 112 years, and Rugby Sevens makes its debut at the Rio Games.

events.title: Tokyo 2020: Skateboarding Debut
events.description: Skateboarding makes its highly anticipated Olympic debut in Tokyo, appealing to a younger audience.

events.title: Beijing 2022: Women's Monobob Debut
events.description: The women's monobob event makes its Olympic debut, with Kaillie Humphries winning the first gold.

events.title: First Olympic Village (Paris 1924)
events.description: The first Olympic Village is constructed for the Paris Games, consisting of small wooden cabins.

events.title: Hans-Gunnar Liljenwall: First Doping DQ
events.description: The Swedish pentathlete becomes the first person to be disqualified from the Olympics for doping (alcohol).

events.title: Baron Pierre de Coubertin Dies
events.description: The founder of the modern Olympics dies in Geneva; his heart is buried in Olympia, Greece.

events.title: First Olympic Mascot: Schuss
events.description: The unofficial mascot 'Schuss' appears at the Grenoble Winter Games, starting a long-standing tradition.
